title: Personality and eating disorders
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's personality or eating disorder.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for weight management and eating habits.

HPI
The patient is a 55-year-old man presenting for a follow-up evaluation of his eating disorder. He was previously diagnosed with anorexia nervosa, specifically the restricting type. He reports that he continues to struggle with consistent caloric intake and expresses ongoing concerns regarding his weight fluctuations. He notes that while he is attending his scheduled appointments, he finds it difficult to adhere to the suggested meal plans consistently. He describes his current status as moderate in terms of his difficulty maintaining a balanced nutritional intake. He denies any recent physical injuries or acute medical concerns.

Review of Systems
The patient reports no chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations. He denies fever, chills, or night sweats. He reports no recent changes in bowel habits or urinary frequency. He denies any significant joint pain or muscle weakness.

Social History
The patient is currently employed full-time and lives with his spouse. He enjoys hiking and watching films in his spare time. He denies any tobacco use.

Family History
His father has hypertension. His mother has type 2 diabetes. There is a family history of cardiovascular disease.

Medication List
Multivitamin (daily)
Vitamin D3 2000 IU (daily)

Vitals
Blood Pressure: 128/82 mmHg
Heart Rate: 74 bpm
Temperature: 98.6 F
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Weight: 142 lbs
Height: 5'10"

Recent Labs
Hemoglobin: 13.2 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 6.5 x 10^9/L
Glucose: 98 mg/dL
eGFR: 88 mL/min/1.73m2

Exam
The patient appears well-nourished but thin. He is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. Skin is dry but intact. Heart sounds are regular with no murmurs. Lungs are clear to auscultation. Abdomen is soft, non-tender, and non-distended.

Assessment
The patient presents with anorexia nervosa, restricting type. His current symptoms and behaviors are consistent with moderate severity. He remains engaged in his treatment plan but requires continued monitoring of nutritional status.

Plan
1. Continue with current dietitian consultations to address caloric intake.
2. Continue with therapy sessions to address underlying behavioral patterns.
3. Follow up in four weeks to monitor weight and progress.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, PA-C
May 14, 2026
explanations: Anorexia nervosa, restricting type, moderate: F50.011 (HCC 153).

distractors.why: The type and severity are documented.
The restricting type is documented, not binge-purge.
